checks: No eclipse at 46 of 134 covered epochs where the 1.18563 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 59388389 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.53% occurring every 1.1856 days, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 65.7 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis via difference imaging confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 28.3 and a centroid offset of 0.7 arcsec. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued object. While the machine learning screening score of 0.44 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real stellar target, continued observation would help establish the nature and properties of this system.
